title: Polynomial mixing of the switch chain for every graphical degree sequence
summary: We prove the simple-undirected form of the Kannan–Tetali–Vempala conjecture: the switch chain on simple undirected graphs mixes in polynomial time for every graphical degree sequence. For a lazy chain that proposes switches uniformly on four vertices, the total-variation mixing time at distance 1/4 is at most $`2n^8`$. We also give an exactly uniform sampler for every graphical labeled degree vector. It uses unbiased random bits, terminates almost surely, and has expected polynomial bit running time.
family_title: Rapid mixing of graph switches for every degree sequence

review.reason: Proves polynomial mixing of the switch chain and gives an exactly uniform graph sampler.

discussion.text: Rapid mixing of graph switches for every degree sequence: I worked on this one in a team. I recall that we were all convinced that it's rapidly mixing. Glad that OpenAI finally proved it!
